text:
Maria Chen: quick sync — we need to pick a sessionization approach for billing events. PMs want per-session billing windows (session = user interaction window) so we can split long-running streams into smaller billable chunks.
Zach Patel: so two problems: assign events to sessions (real-time) and reconcile when sessions close late or cross devices.
Lee Gomez: +1. also need dedupe semantics for retransmits and reconnects.
Anjali Rao: proposal i sketched earlier: assign a session_id at first request, keep session_ttl (idle timeout) and emit a session_close event when TTL expires. billing events map to active session_id. reconciliation job stitches late closes.
Maria Chen: tradeoffs?
Zach Patel: if we rely on client-generated session_id we avoid server allocation cost but clients are buggy. server-generated ids are authoritative but add a roundtrip.
Lee Gomez: design we discussed: accept client session_id but validate/normalize on ingress. If missing, server mints. Use a short namespace prefix to avoid collisions.
Anjali Rao: dedupe key: "session_id|event_seq|event_type". store low-cardinality index for last_seq per-session for quick in-flight dedupe.
Maria Chen: how do we handle late-arriving events that should retroactively change billing attribution? e.g., session extends beyond TTL because of sporadic pings.
Zach Patel: keep raw events for 30 days. nightly recon job compares final session boundaries and emits compensation events if tokens shift between billing windows. Compensation events are tagged with original_event_ids.
Lee Gomez: cost concern: indexing every raw event is heavy. compromise: keep a compacted event log per session (append-only, compressed) plus pointers to the first/last event ids. Recon uses compacted log unless we need full fidelity.
Anjali Rao: metrics + invariants: 1) real-time meter must be <=200ms ingest-to-credit lookup 2) recon can be eventual but must converge within 24h for invoices 3) compensation events must be idempotent.
Maria Chen: what about query patterns for support/debugging? we need to quickly answer "what was billed for session X".
Zach Patel: materialize a session-billing snapshot after recon (s3 parquet + small lookup DB). Snapshot keys: session_id, tenant_id, window_start, window_end, billed_tokens, reconciliation_state.
Lee Gomez: fallback behavior: if recon job finds missing raw events (expired), mark reconciliation_state=partial and surface to ops. Avoid silent billing changes.
Anjali Rao: operational playbook: metering-bot posts a nightly summary in #eng-platform with counts of reconciled sessions, compensation events emitted, and top N tenants with adjustments.
metering-bot: nightly-recon finished: reconciled_sessions=3,201 compensation_events=42 top_tenants=[acme,globex] (run-id: r-2026-03-20)
Maria Chen: ok plan: implement validation layer (accept-or-mint session_id), session compacted-log retention 30d, recon job producing compensation events within 24h, snapshot materialization for queries. We'll draft RFC for interface and storage costs.
Zach Patel: I'll prototype ingress normalizer and small in-memory last_seq cache for dedupe.
Lee Gomez: I'll run a cheap simulation to estimate index size for compacted logs.
Anjali Rao: i'll own the recon job + compensation schema.
Maria Chen: thanks — can we have follow-up RFC by EOD Thursday? short doc + data size estimate.
Zach Patel: yes. Ping me if you want a quick pairing session.
Lee Gomez: thumbs-up :thumbsup:
